questions.question: A certain sum of money becomes seven times itself when invested at a certain rate of simple interest, in 14 years. How much time (in years, rounded off to 2 decimal places) will it take to become 18 times itself at the same rate?
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum of money becomes seven times itself when invested at a certain rate of simple interest, in 14 years. How much time (in years, rounded off to 2 decimal places) will it take to become 18 times itself at the same rate?
questions.solution:
7P = P + (P × R × 14) / 100

⇒ 6P = 14PR / 100

⇒ R = 42.86%

Find time for sum to become 18 times:

18P = P + (P × 42.86 × T) / 100

⇒ 17P = 0.4286PT

⇒ T = 39.67 years

questions.question: A sum of money becomes three times of itself at the rate of 10 percent per annum on simple interest. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct? I. It will become 5 times of itself at the rate of 20 percent per annum on simple interest in the same time period. II. It will become 7 times of itself at the rate of 30 percent per annum on simple interest in the same time period.
questions.questionHtml:
A sum of money becomes three times of itself at the rate of 10 percent per annum on simple interest. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?

I. It will become 5 times of itself at the rate of 20 percent per annum on simple interest in the same time period.

II. It will become 7 times of itself at the rate of 30 percent per annum on simple interest in the same time period.
questions.solution:
Calculation:

The formula for simple interest is:

I = PRT/100,

where:
I = interest earned,

P = principal amount (initial investment),

R = annual interest rate (in percentage),

T = time (in years).

If a sum of money becomes three times of itself at a rate of 10 percent per annum, it means that twice the initial sum was earned as interest (because the initial sum plus twice the sum gives three times the sum). So:

2P = PRT/100

Substituting the given R = 10, we get:

2P = P × 10 × T/100

Solving for T:

T = 2 × 100/10 = 20 years.

Now, for the two statements:

I. For the money to become 5 times of itself at the rate of 20 percent per annum in the same time period (20 years), the interest earned must be four times the principal. So:

4P = P × 20 ×T/100 = P× 20 × 20/100 = 4P.

So, Statement I is correct.

II. For the money to become 7 times of itself at the rate of 30 percent per annum in the same time period (20 years), the interest earned must be six times the principal. So:

6P = P × 30 × T/100 = P × 30 × 20/100 = 6P.

So, Statement II is also correct.

Thus, both statements I and II are correct.

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 17,200 is lent out at simple interest in two parts for 2 years at 8% p.a. and 10% p.a., respectively, if the total interest received after 2 years is Rs. 3,008, then the money lent (in Rs.) at the rate of 8% p.a. is:

questions.solution:
Let the amount lent on 8 % be a

⇒ Amount on 10 % = (17,200 - a)

SI on principal “a” = (a x 8 x 2) / 100 = \(4a\over 25\)

Similarly, SI on principal (17,200 - a) = \((17,200 - a) × 10 × 2\over 100\) = \(17,200 – a \over 5\)

According to the question, total interest accrued was Rs 3008

⇒ \(4a\over 25\) + \(17,200 – a \over 5\) = 3008

⇒ 4a + 86,000 - 5a = 3008 ×  25

⇒ a = Rs 10,800

questions.question: Ramu invested some money at 8% simple interest per annum, and it was grown up to Rs. 820 in 8 years. If the same sum was invested at 20% simple interest per annum for a period of 10 years, find the amount.
questions.questionHtml: <!-- x-tinymce/html -->Ramu invested some money at 8% simple interest per annum, and it was grown up to Rs. 820 in 8 years. If the same sum was invested at 20% simple interest per annum for a period of 10 years, find the amount.
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal (P) at 8% = Amount (A) - Interest (SI)

Amount (A) = ₹820

Time (t) = 8 years

Rate (r) = 8%

Formula used:

Simple Interest (SI) = P × r × t / 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

Calculations:

820 = P + (P × 8 × 8 / 100)

⇒ 820 = P + (64P / 100)

⇒ 820 = P (1 + 0.64)

⇒ 820 = P × 1.64

⇒ P = 820 / 1.64

⇒ P = ₹500

Now, for 20% interest for 10 years:

Rate (r) = 20%

Time (t) = 10 years

Simple Interest (SI) = P × r × t / 100

⇒ SI = 500 × 20 × 10 / 100

⇒ SI = ₹1000

Amount (A) = P + SI

⇒ A = 500 + 1000

⇒ A = ₹1500

∴ The correct answer is option (3).

questions.question: The rate of simple interest for first two years is 8% p.a., for the next 4 years, it is 10% p.a. and for the period beyond 6 years, it is 12% p.a. If a person gets Rs. 18358.60 as simple interest after 9 years, then how much money (in Rs.) did he invest?
questions.questionHtml: The rate of simple interest for first two years is 8% p.a., for the next 4 years, it is 10% p.a. and for the period beyond 6 years, it is 12% p.a. If a person gets Rs. 18358.60 as simple interest after 9 years, then how much money (in Rs.) did he invest?

Given:

Total interest after 9 years = Rs. 18358.60

Formula used:

SI = (P × R × T)100

Calculation:

Let the principal be P

For the first 2 years

SI = P × 8 × 2/100

⇒ 4P/25

For the next 4 years

SI = P × 4 × 10/100

⇒ 2P/5

For the next 3 years

SI = P × 3 × 12/100

⇒ 9P/25

Total interest in 9 years =  Rs. 18358.60

⇒ (4P/25 + 2P/5 + 9P/25) = 18358.60

⇒ 23P/25 = 18358.60

⇒ P = 19955

∴ The amount invested is Rs. 19955

questions.question: Simple interest on a certain sum is one-fourth of the sum and the interest rate percentage per annum is 4 times the number of years. If the rate of interest increases by 2%, then what will be the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹5,000 for 3 years?
questions.questionHtml: Simple interest on a certain sum is one-fourth of the sum and the interest rate percentage per annum is 4 times the number of years. If the rate of interest increases by 2%, then what will be the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹5,000 for 3 years?
questions.solution:
Let, Amount = 1 then simple interest = 1/4, the rate of interest = R then, time = R/4 years

Now, 1/4 = [1 × R × (R/4)]/100 ⇒ 1/4 = R2/400 ⇒ R = √100 = 10%

The new rate of interest = 10 + 2 = 12%. Total interest for 3 years = 3 × 12 = 36%
The total simple interest = (36/100) × 5000 = 1800

questions.question: On simple interest, a certain sum becomes Rs. 59,200 in 6 years and Rs. 72,000 in 10 years. If the rate of interest had been 2% more, then in how many years would the sum have become RS. 76,000?
questions.questionHtml: On simple interest, a certain sum becomes Rs. 59,200 in 6 years and Rs. 72,000 in 10 years. If the rate of interest had been 2% more, then in how many years would the sum have become RS. 76,000?
questions.solution:
The total interest in 4 years = 72000 - 59200 = Rs. 12800 and in 6 years = (12800/4) × 6 = Rs. 19200. So, the total amount = 59200 - 19200 = Rs. 40000

The rate of interest had been 2% more: 40000 × (2/100) = Rs. 800

The new total interest in 1 year = (12800/4) + 800 = Rs. 4000
The required interest = 76000 - 40000 = Rs. 36000
So, the time required = 36000/4000 = 9 years

questions.question: What is the difference (in Rs.) between the simple interest and the compound interest on a sum of Rs. 8000 for \(2\frac{2}{5}\) years at the rate of 10% p.a. when the interest is compounded yearly?
questions.questionHtml: What is the difference (in Rs.) between the simple interest and the compound interest on a sum of Rs. 8000 for \(2\frac{2}{5}\) years at the rate of 10% p.a. when the interest is compounded yearly?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Net Simple Interest (SI) rate for 2.4 years at 10% = 10% × 2.4 = 24%.

Successive rates for Compound Interest (CI): 10%, 10%, and (10 × 2/5)% = 4%.

Net CI rate = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = 21%; then 21 + 4 + (21 × 4)/100 = 25.84%.

Difference in percentage = 25.84% − 24% = 1.84%.

Difference in value = 1.84% of ₹8000 = 80 × 1.84 = ₹147.20.

∴ The correct answer is ₹147.20.

Alternate Method

Given: Principal (P) = ₹8000, Rate (R) = 10% p.a., Time (T) = 22/5 years = 2.4 years.

Formula Used: SI = (P × R × T) / 100 | CI Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)n

⇒ Simple Interest (SI) = (8000 × 10 × 2.4) / 100

⇒ SI = 80 × 24 = ₹1920

⇒ Compound Interest Amount (A) = 8000 × (1 + 10/100) × (1 + 10/100) × (1 + 4/100)

⇒ A = 8000 × 1.1 × 1.1 × 1.04

⇒ A = 8000 × 1.21 × 1.04 = 9680 × 1.04 = ₹10067.20

⇒ Compound Interest (CI) = 10067.20 − 8000 = ₹2067.20

⇒ Difference = 2067.20 − 1920 = ₹147.20

∴ The correct answer is ₹147.20.

Additional Information

CI and SI Difference (2 Years)

For a period of 2 years, the difference is calculated as: Diff = P(R/100)2.

CI and SI Difference (3 Years)

For a period of 3 years, the difference is: Diff = P(R/100)2 × (3 + R/100).

Fractional Time Period CI

If time is T = n + a/b years, Amount = P(1 + R/100)n × (1 + (a/b × R)/100).

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 27,000 is divided into two parts A and B such that the simple interest at the rate of 15% p.a. on A and B after two years and four years, respectively, is equal. The total interest (in Rs.) received together from A and B is:
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 27,000 is divided into two parts A and B such that the simple interest at the rate of 15% p.a. on A and B after two years and four years, respectively, is equal. The total interest (in Rs.) received together from A and B is:
questions.solution:
Given:

A sum divided into A and B = Rs 27,000

Rate of simple interest = 15%

A invests for 2 years and B invests for 4 years

Formula Used:

SI = P × R × T/100

Calculation:

Let the sum of A be x

Then, the sum of B be (27,000 - x)

SI of A for 2 years = x × 2 × 15/100

⇒ 30x/100

SI of B for 4 years = (27,000 - x) × 4 × 15/100

⇒ (27,000 - x) × 60/100

⇒ 27000 × 60/100 - 60x/100

⇒ 16200 - 60x/100

According to the question:

SI of A = SI of B

⇒ 30x/100 = 16200 - 60x/100

⇒ 90x/100 = 16200

⇒ x = 18000

Sum of A = Rs 18,000

Sum of B = Rs (27,000 - 18,000) = Rs 9,000

SI of A = 30x/100 = 30 × 18000/100 = Rs 5400

SI of A = SI of B = Rs 5400

Total interest of A and B = 5400 + 5400 = Rs 10800

∴ Total interest of A and B is Rs 10800.

questions.question: A bank charges simple interest for Rs. K at the rate of \(\rm r^{\frac{1}{2}}\) for n 2 years. Another bank charges simple interest for Rs. L at the rate of \(\rm r^{\frac{3}{2}}\) for n 3 years and gives the same interest. The ratio between K and L is:
questions.questionHtml: A bank charges simple interest for Rs. K at the rate of \(\rm r^{\frac{1}{2}}\) for n2 years. Another bank charges simple interest for Rs. L at the rate of \(\rm r^{\frac{3}{2}}\) for n3 years and gives the same interest. The ratio between K and L is:
questions.solution:
K × r1/2 × n2 / 100 = L × r3/2 × n3 / 100

K × r1/2 × n2 = L × r3/2 × n3

K / L = r3/2 - 1/2 × n3 - 2, ⇒ K / L = r × n , ⇒ K / L = rn

questions.question: A certain sum becomes 4 times of itself in 5 years at a rate of simple interest. In 15 years it will become how many times of itself at the same rate of simple interest?
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum becomes 4 times of itself in 5 years at a rate of simple interest. In 15 years it will become how many times of itself at the same rate of simple interest?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In Simple Interest, the interest earned is directly proportional to the time period.

Direct Formula: (n1 − 1) ÷ t1 = (n2 − 1) ÷ t2

Given: n1 = 4, t1 = 5 years, t2 = 15 years.

⇒ (4 − 1) ÷ 5 = (n2 − 1) ÷ 15

⇒ 3 ÷ 5 = (n2 − 1) ÷ 15 ⇒ n2 − 1 = 9 ⇒ n2 = 10

∴ The correct answer is 10 times.

Alternate Method

Given:

A sum becomes 4 times of itself in 5 years at simple interest.

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

Calculations:

⇒ Let the principal sum be P.

⇒ Amount after 5 years = 4P

⇒ Simple Interest earned in 5 years = 4P − P = 3P

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T)

⇒ R = (3P × 100) ÷ (P × 5) = 60%

⇒ Now, we need to find the amount after T = 15 years at R = 60%:

⇒ SI = (P × 60 × 15) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 900P ÷ 100 = 9P

⇒ New Amount = Principal + SI = P + 9P = 10P

⇒ Thus, the sum will become 10 times of itself.

∴ The correct answer is 10 times.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Constant Growth

Unlike compound interest, simple interest grows by a constant amount every year. If a sum earns 3P interest in 5 years, it will earn exactly 3P interest in every subsequent 5-year period.

Direct Formula for Multipliers

When a sum becomes n1 times in t1 years and n2 times in t2 years at simple interest, use the relation: (n1 − 1) ÷ t1 = (n2 − 1) ÷ t2.

Principal and Amount Relation

The amount (A) is the sum of Principal (P) and Simple Interest (SI). Always subtract 1 from the number of times it becomes to get the interest multiplier: SI = (n − 1)P.

questions.question: A sum lent at simple interest amounts to Rs.6,240.80 in one year and to Rs.7,563.20 in 4 years. The sum (in Rs.) and the rate of interest per annum, respectively, are:
questions.questionHtml: A sum lent at simple interest amounts to Rs.6,240.80 in one year and to Rs.7,563.20 in 4 years. The sum (in Rs.) and the rate of interest per annum, respectively, are:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since Simple Interest is constant every year, SI for 3 years = Amount4 − Amount1

⇒ 3 years SI = 7563.20 − 6240.80 = ₹1322.40

⇒ 1 year SI = 1322.40 ÷ 3 = ₹440.80

⇒ Principal = 6240.80 − 440.80 = ₹5800

⇒ Rate = (440.80 ÷ 5800) × 100 = 7.6%

∴ The correct answer is ₹5800, 7.6%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Amount after 1 year (A1) = ₹6240.80

Amount after 4 years (A4) = ₹7563.20

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

Calculations:

⇒ SI for 3 years = A4 − A1

⇒ SI for 3 years = 7563.20 − 6240.80 = 1322.40

⇒ SI for 1 year = 1322.40 ÷ 3 = 440.80

⇒ Principal (P) = A1 − SI for 1 year

⇒ P = 6240.80 − 440.80 = 5800

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (SI for 1 year × 100) ÷ P

⇒ R = (440.80 × 100) ÷ 5800

⇒ R = 44080 ÷ 5800 = 7.6%

∴ The correct answer is ₹5800, 7.6%.

Additional Information

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the principal remains constant every year, meaning the interest generated is the same annually. In Compound Interest, the accumulated interest of past periods is added to the principal to form the base for the next period.

Principal from Amounts Rule

If a principal becomes A1 in T1 years and A2 in T2 years under Simple Interest, the principal can be directly calculated as P = A1 − [ (A2 − A1) ÷ (T2 − T1) ] × T1.

Constant SI Property

Since Simple Interest does not compound, the interest accrued over any N-year period is always directly proportional to N, making it uniformly additive.

questions.question: A sum of money was lent in two parts in the ratio 4 ∶ 5 for 4 years and 5 years respectively, both at the rate of 8% per annum simple interest. If the difference between the interests earned from the two parts is Rs.4680, then what was the total sum lent (in Rs.)?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of money was lent in two parts in the ratio 4 ∶ 5 for 4 years and 5 years respectively, both at the rate of 8% per annum simple interest. If the difference between the interests earned from the two parts is Rs.4680, then what was the total sum lent (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
Given:

The ratio of sum of money = 4 : 5

T1 = 4 years

T2 = 5 years

Rate = 8%

Difference between the interests earned from the two parts = Rs. 4680

Formula used:

SI = (P × R × T)/100

Calculation:

Let the ratio of sum of money be 4x and 5x respectively

Total ratio of sum of money = (4x + 5x) = 9x

According to the question

SI on first part = (4x × 8 × 4)/100

⇒ 128x/100

SI on second part = (5x × 8 × 5)/100

⇒ 200x/100

Difference between the interests = (200x/100 – 128x/100)

⇒ 72x/100

Now,

⇒ 72x/100 = 4680

⇒ 72x = (4680 × 100)

⇒ 72x = 468000

⇒ x = (468000/72)

⇒ x = Rs. 6500

The total sum lent = 9x = Rs. (9 × 6500)

⇒ Rs. 58500

∴ The required total sum lent is Rs. 58500

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 12,000 was taken at simple interest at some rate. After four months, Rs. 6,000 more was added and the total principal was charged at double the earlier rate of interest. At the end of the year, if the total interest was Rs. 2,800, what was the initial rate of interest?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 12,000 was taken at simple interest at some rate. After four months, Rs. 6,000 more was added and the total principal was charged at double the earlier rate of interest. At the end of the year, if the total interest was Rs. 2,800, what was the initial rate of interest?
questions.solution:
Given:

Case-1

Principal = 12,000

Rate = r%

Time = 4 month

Case-2

Principal = (12,000 + 6,000) = 18,000

Rate = 2r%

Time = 8 months

Total SI = Rs. 2800

Formula:

SI = Prt/100

Calculation:

According to the formula

2800 = [(12,000 × r × 4/12)/100] + [(18,000 × 2r × 8/12)/100]

⇒ 2800 = 40r + 240r

⇒ 280r = 2800

⇒ r = 2800/280

⇒ r = 10%

∴ The initial rate of interest was 10%.

questions.question: In a bank, 6% interest is given on the deposited amount. The bank then invests the money in the stock market and is able to earn ₹30,000 for every ₹3,00,000. How much money is the bank earning finally if the total amount deposited in the bank is ₹60,00,000?
questions.questionHtml: In a bank, 6% interest is given on the deposited amount. The bank then invests the money in the stock market and is able to earn ₹30,000 for every ₹3,00,000. How much money is the bank earning finally if the total amount deposited in the bank is ₹60,00,000?
questions.solution:
Interest earned by the depositors:

⇒ ₹60,00,000 × 0.06

⇒ ₹3,60,000

Profit earned from the stock market:

⇒ (₹60,00,000 / ₹3,00,000) × ₹30,000

⇒ ₹6,00,000

Total earning of the bank:

⇒ ₹6,00,000 - ₹3,60,000

⇒ ₹2,40,000

questions.solution:
Let P be the principal amount.

SI = P/5 and R = 5T

questions.question: A person invested a sum of Rs. 25,000 in two parts. First part at 10% per annum simple interest and the rest at 12% per annum simple interest. At the end of 2 years, the total interest received was Rs. 5,640. The difference (in Rs.) between the two parts of the sum is:
questions.questionHtml: A person invested a sum of Rs. 25,000 in two parts. First part at 10% per annum simple interest and the rest at 12% per annum simple interest. At the end of 2 years, the total interest received was Rs. 5,640. The difference (in Rs.) between the two parts of the sum is:
questions.solution:
Given:          

Total invested = Rs. 25000

Two interest is 10% and 12%

Total interest = Rs. 5640

Formula used:

Simple Interest = {Sum (P) × rate of interest (r) × time (t)}/100

Calculation:

Let the sum at 10% be x

Then the sum at 12%  = (25000 – x)

S.I at 10% rate = 10 × x × 2/100 = x/5

S.I at 12% rate =  12 × (25000 – x) × 2/100

⇒ 6 × (25000 – x)/25

Total Simple interest = 5640

⇒ x/5 + [6 × (25000 – x)/25] = 5640

⇒ [5x + 150000 – 6x]/25 = 5640

⇒ -x + 150000 = 141000 

⇒ x = 9000

The sum lent at S.I rate 10% per annum is Rs. 9000.

And the sum lent at S.I rate 12% per annum is Rs. 16000.

So, the difference between them = 16000 – 9000 = Rs. 7000 

∴ The difference between them is Rs. 7000.

questions.question: A certain sum of money amounts to ₹1,250 in 4 years and to ₹1,520 in \(5 \frac{1}{2}\) years at a certain rate of simple interest. Find the rate of interest per annum (correct to two places of decimals).
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum of money amounts to ₹1,250 in 4 years and to ₹1,520 in \(5 \frac{1}{2}\) years at a certain rate of simple interest. Find the rate of interest per annum (correct to two places of decimals).
questions.solution:
Given:

A certain sum of money amounts to ₹1,250 in 4 years and to ₹1,520 in 51/2 years at a certain rate of simple interest.

Formula used:

Simple Interest (SI) = P × R × T / 100

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

Calculation:

Let the principal be P and the rate of interest be R%.

For 4 years:

1250 = P + P × R × 4 / 100

For 51/2 years:

1520 = P + P × R × 11 / 2 / 100

From the first equation:

1250 = P (1 + 4R / 100)

⇒ 1250 = P (1 + R / 25)

From the second equation:

1520 = P (1 + 11R / 200)

⇒ 1520 = P (1 + 11R / 200)

Divide the second equation by the first equation:

1520 / 1250 = (1 + 11R / 200) / (1 + R / 25)

⇒ 1.216 = (1 + 11R / 200) / (1 + R / 25)

Cross-multiply to solve for R:

1.216 × (1 + R / 25) = 1 + 11R / 200

⇒ 1.216 + 1.216R / 25 = 1 + 11R / 200

⇒ 1.216 + 0.04864R = 1 + 0.055R

⇒ 0.216 = 0.00636R

⇒ R = 0.216 / 0.00636

⇒ R ≈ 33.96%

∴ The correct answer is option (2).

questions.question: A man took a loan of Rs. 32,400 at a certain rate of simple interest per annum. The rate of interest is one-fourth of the number of years for which the loan is taken. If he paid Rs. 11,664 as interest at the end of the loan period, the rate of interest was:
questions.questionHtml: A man took a loan of Rs. 32,400 at a certain rate of simple interest per annum. The rate of interest is one-fourth of the number of years for which the loan is taken. If he paid Rs. 11,664 as interest at the end of the loan period, the rate of interest was:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the Rate of Interest be R. Then Time T = 4R.

Using the direct relation: R2 = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × 4)

R2 = (11664 × 100) ÷ (32400 × 4) = 11664 ÷ 1296 = 9

R = √9 = 3%

∴ The correct answer is 3%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = ₹32,400

Simple Interest (SI) = ₹11,664

Rate (R) = T ÷ 4 ⇒ Time (T) = 4R years

Calculations:

⇒ SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 11,664 = (32,400 × R × 4R) ÷ 100

⇒ 11,664 = 324 × 4R2

⇒ 11,664 = 1,296R2

⇒ R2 = 11,664 ÷ 1,296

⇒ R2 = 9

⇒ R = √9 = 3

∴ The correct answer is 3%.

questions.question: Two equal sum (in Rs.) are lent at 8% and 4% simple interest p.a. respectively at the same time. The first sum is received 2 years earlier than the other and the amount received in each case is Rs. 14,500. Each sum is:
questions.questionHtml: Two equal sum (in Rs.) are lent at 8% and 4% simple interest p.a. respectively at the same time. The first sum is received 2 years earlier than the other and the amount received in each case is Rs. 14,500. Each sum is:
questions.solution:
Given:

P1 = P2, R1 = 8% and R2 = 4%

The first sum is collected 2 years earlier than the second

Formula used:

SI = (P × R × T)/100

Calculation:

Let Principal be p and time be t

According to the question

p + (p × 8 × t)/100 = p + (p × 4 × (t + 2)/100

8pt = 4pt + 8p

8p = 4pt

t = 8p/4p = 2

t = 2 years, r = 8%

As we know,

p + prt/100 = Amount

p + (p × 8 × 2)/100 = 14500

116p/100 = 14500

p = 14500 × 100/116

p = 12500

∴ The correct answer is 12500

Shortcut Trick Let P be the sum in both cases

Also, let time for the first amount be T years

⇒ Time for the second amount is (T + 2) years

Both Amounts are equal

⇒ 8T% of P = 4(T + 2)% of P

⇒ 8T = 4T + 8

⇒ T = 2 years

Now, amount = 14500, R = 8%, and T = 2 years

⇒ 116% of P = 14500

⇒ P = 12500

∴ The correct answer is 12500

questions.question: A person invested a sum of Rs. 10,500 at x% per annum at simple interest and a sum of Rs. 13,500 at (x + 2)% p.a. at simple interest. If the total interest earned on both the investments for 3 years is Rs. 7,650, then the rate of interest on the first investment is:

315x + 405x + 810 = 7650

720x = 7650 – 810 = 6840

x = 6840/720 = 9.5%

Required rate = 9.5%

questions.questionHtml: Two equal sums are lent at 10% and 8% simple interest p.a. respectively, at the same time. The first sum is received 2 years earlier than the second one and the amount received in each case was Rs. 36,900. Each sum was ______.
questions.solution:

According to the question

2t = 16

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 25600 is invested on simple interest partly at 7% per annum and the remaining at 9% per annum. The total interest at the end of 3 years is Rs. 5832. How much money (in Rs.) was invested at 9% per annum?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 25600 is invested on simple interest partly at 7% per annum and the remaining at 9% per annum. The total interest at the end of 3 years is Rs. 5832. How much money (in Rs.) was invested at 9% per annum?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick 

Interest for one year = 5832/3 = Rs. 1944

Interest for 7% = 25600 × 7/100 = 1792

Interest for 9% = 25600 × 9/100 = 2304

The sum invested on 9%

= 152/(360 + 152) × 25600

= 152/512 × 25600 = Rs. 7600

 Alternate Method

Given:

Sum = Rs. 25600

R1 = 7%

R2 = 9%

The total interest at the end of 3 years = Rs. 5832

Formula used:

SI = (P × R × T)/100

Calculation:

Let the principal be x

Then,

A sum of Rs. 25600 is invested on SI at (25600 – x)

The total interest at the end of 3 years = Rs. 5832

The total interest at the end of 1 year = Rs. (5832/3)

⇒ Rs. 1944

Now,

According to the question

⇒ (x × 1 × 9)/100 + [(25600 – x) × 1 × 7]/100 = 1944

⇒ 9x/100 + (179200 – 7x)/100 = 1944

⇒ 9x + 179200 – 7x = 194400

⇒ (9x – 7x) = (194400 – 179200)

⇒ 2x = 15200

⇒ x = (15200/2)

⇒ x = 7600

∴ The money invested at 9% per annum is Rs. 7600

questions.question: A person borrows Rs. 20000 at the rate of 6 percent per annum on simple interest for 3 years. He immediately lends it to another person at the rate of 8.5 percent per annum on simple interest for 3 years. What is the value of gain per year?
questions.questionHtml: A person borrows Rs. 20000 at the rate of 6 percent per annum on simple interest for 3 years. He immediately lends it to another person at the rate of 8.5 percent per annum on simple interest for 3 years. What is the value of gain per year?
questions.solution:
Given:

A person borrows Rs. 20000 for 3 years at 6% per annum Simple Interest.

He immediately lends it to another person at 8.5% per annum for 3 years.

Formula Used:

Simple Interest = PRT/100

Where, P = Principal, R = Rate and T = Time 

Calculation:

P = Rs. 20000 and time = 3 years

First rate = 6% and Second rate = 8.5%

As we know,

SI = Prt/100

⇒ [20000 × (8.5 - 6) × 1]/100

⇒ [20000 × 2.5 × 1]/100

⇒  500

∴ His gain in the transaction per year is 500

 Shortcut Trick

Difference of rate for 1 years = 8.5% - 6% = 2.5%

The gain in the transaction for 1 year = 20000 × 2.5/100 = 500

questions.question: Sudeep invested 1/8 of a certain sum at 5% per annum for two years and 3/5 of the sum of 6% per annum for two years and the remaining at 10% p.a. for two years. If the total interest received is Rs. 1,674, then the total sum invested is:
questions.questionHtml: Sudeep invested 1/8 of a certain sum at 5% per annum for two years and 3/5 of the sum of 6% per annum for two years and the remaining at 10% p.a. for two years. If the total interest received is Rs. 1,674, then the total sum invested is:

As we know,

Simple Interest = PRT/100

Let total sum be Rs. x, then

Remaining part = x - x/8 - 3x/5 = (40x - 5x - 24x)/40 = 11x/40

According to the question

(x × 1/8 × 5 × 2)/100 + (x × 3/5 × 6 × 2)/100 + (x × 11/40 × 10 × 2)/100 = 1674

5x/400 + 36x/500 + 11x/200 = 1674

(25x + 144x + 110x)/2000 = 1674

279x/2000 = 1674

x = 1674 × 2000/279

x = 12000

Alternate Solution:

Let total number be 40x, then

As we know,

40x × 1/8 = 5x and 40x × 3/5 = 24x and 40x - 5x - 24x = 11x

According to the question

[2 × (5x × 5 + 24x × 6 + 11x × 10)]/100 = 1674

2 × 279x = 167400

558x = 167400

x = 167400/558

x = 300

Total sum = 40 × 300 = 12000

questions.question: A sum is deposited in a bank which gives simple interest. The sum becomes 1.25 times in 3 years. If there is a requirement of ₹7,60,000 after seven years, how much amount (in ₹) should one deposit to fulfil the requirement?

questions.question: A certain sum amounts to Rs. 81840 in 3 years and to Rs. 92400 in 5 years at x% p.a. under simple interest. If the rate of interest is becomes (x + 2)%, then in how many years will the same sum double itself?
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum amounts to Rs. 81840 in 3 years and to Rs. 92400 in 5 years at x% p.a. under simple interest. If the rate of interest is becomes (x + 2)%, then in how many years will the same sum double itself?
questions.solution:
Given:

A certain sum amounts to Rs. 81840 in 3 years

And to Rs. 92400 in 5 years

Rate of interest = x %

Concept used:

S.I. = PRT/100

S.I. = Simple Interest

P= Principal

R = Rate of interest

T = Time in years

Amount = P + S.I.

Calculation:

S.I. for 2 years = 92400 - 81840 = 10560 Rs.

S.I. for 1 year = 10560/2 = 5280 Rs.

S.I for 3 years = 5280 × 3 = 15840 Rs

So, the principal = 81840 - 15840

⇒ 66000 Rs.

Now,

(66000 × x × 3)/100 = 15840

⇒ x = 8

Now, if the rate of interest is 8 + 2 = 10% p.a. the sum doubles itself.

Let the sum doubles itself in t years. If Principal = x then Amount = 2x

So, Interest = Amount - Principal = 2x - x = x
      Interest = Principal 

(66000 × 10 × t)/100 = 66000

⇒ t = 10

∴ The same sum will double itself in 10 years.

questions.question: At a certain annual rate (rounded off to the nearest integer) of simple interest, a sum of money becomes nine times its original value in 21 years. By how much does the rate of interest change if the same sum of money has to become 12 times its original value in 25 years?
questions.questionHtml: At a certain annual rate (rounded off to the nearest integer) of simple interest, a sum of money becomes nine times its original value in 21 years. By how much does the rate of interest change if the same sum of money has to become 12 times its original value in 25 years?

RT = (n - 1)100

⇒ R = 800/21 = 38%

And,

⇒ R × 25 = 11 × 100

⇒ R = 1100/25 = 44%

Difference = 44 - 38 = 6%

∴ The correct answer is 6%.

questions.question: A certain sum invested at simple interest amounts to Rs. 10,072 in \(3\frac{1}{2}\) years and to Rs. 11,552 in 6 years at the same rate per annum. The rate of interest p.a. is:
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum invested at simple interest amounts to Rs. 10,072 in \(3\frac{1}{2}\) years and to Rs. 11,552 in 6 years at the same rate per annum. The rate of interest p.a. is:
questions.solution:
Formula:

R = \(SI \times 100\over P\times T\)

P = A - SI, where

P = Principal

R = Rate

T = Time

SI = Simple Interest

A = Amount.

Calculation:

Interest for ( 6 - 3.5 =  \(2\frac{1}{2}\)) years = 11,552 - 10,072 = Rs 1480

⇒ Total interest for 6 year = \(1480\over 2 \frac {1}{2}\) × 6 = 1480 × \(2\over 5\) ×  6 = Rs 3,552

Principal = 11,552 - 3,552 = Rs 8000

R = \(3552 \times 100\over 8000\times 6\) = 7.4%

∴ The rate of interest is 7.4%.

Additional Information Interest for successive years remains constant in Simple Interest. However, Interest varies for Compound Interest for successive years.

questions.question: A sum of Rs.x amounts to Rs.8,563.50 in \(3\frac{1}{2}\) years and to Rs.10,527 in 7 years at y% p.a. simple interest. The value of x and y, respectively, are:
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs.x amounts to Rs.8,563.50 in \(3\frac{1}{2}\) years and to Rs.10,527 in 7 years at y% p.a. simple interest. The value of x and y, respectively, are:
questions.solution:
Given:

Amount1 = Rs. 8,563.50

Time1 = \(3\frac{1}{2}\) years = 7/2 years

Amount2 = Rs. 10,527

Time2 = 7 years

Calculation:

Let the Principal be x and Rate be y respectively

According to the question

SI on Rs. 8,563.50 for (7 – 7/2) years = Rs. (10,527 – 8,563.50)

⇒ 7/2 years = Rs.1,963.50

⇒ 1 year = Rs. (1,963.50 × 2)/7

⇒ 1 year = Rs. 561

Principal = (8,563.50 – 1,963.50) = Rs. 6600

Now,

Rate = (561/6600 × 100)

⇒ (56,100/6600)

⇒ 8.5%

⇒ \(8\frac{1}{2}\)

∴ The value of x and y is 6600 and \(8\frac{1}{2}\)
